title: Proton pump inhibitor and histamine 2 receptor antagonist use and vitamin B12 deficiency
authors: Lam JR, Schneider JL, Zhao W, Corley DA
population: Kaiser Permanente Northern California members: 25,956 with incident vitamin B12 deficiency and 184,199 controls
funder: This project was supported by a Kaiser Permanente Community Benefit grant. Kaiser Permanente had no role in the design and conduct of the study; the collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; the preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; or the decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: Dr Corley reported receiving a grant or grant pending from Wyeth/Pfizer. No other authors reported disclosures.
result: A 2-year or longer supply of PPIs was dispensed to 3120 of 25,956 cases (12.0%) and 13,210 of 184,199 controls (7.2%): OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.58 to 1.73); for H2-receptor antagonists without PPI OR 1.25 (1.17 to 1.34). More than 1.5 PPI pills a day OR 1.95 (1.77 to 2.15) against less than 0.75 pills a day OR 1.63 (1.48 to 1.78).
